jobs.title: What people frame, v
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 21, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, dark hair grown longer. WOOD usually wears brown canvas chore coat with a frayed cuff and one mismatched button, hands in its pockets, plain tee, dark jeans. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Valentine's. A man wants a photo of a woman framed and asks for the cheapest frame. Wood gives him the second cheapest and charges him for the cheapest. The Owner sees. Panel 1: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, a nervous young man at a frame-shop counter holding a snapshot, a young clerk, an older woman at the back (in this panel: WOOD). Customer says "Cheapest one you got. It's — it's just a snapshot.". Wood says "Sure.". Panel 2: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, close-up of a slightly out-of-focus snapshot of a woman laughing. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, a young clerk handing over a black beveled frame while ringing up a lower price, an older woman looking up over her reading glasses from the back (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "Twelve.". Customer says "Sign said fifteen for that one.". Wood says "Sign's old.". Panel 4: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, an older woman tapping a register beside a young clerk, saying something short (in this panel: WOOD). Owner says "Three dollars.". Wood says "Take it out of Friday.". Owner says "I'm not going to. Once.". caption box: "Wednesday.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @supporting is the model sheet for THE EDITOR: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @loc_frame_shop shows the setting; keep its architecture and props. Match the attached references: @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @supporting for the character the editor; @loc_frame_shop for the setting.
